title: Al-An'am
label: Plain-English commentary
intro:
Al-An'am, "The Cattle," is a Makkan surah of one hundred and sixty-five verses. It opens with praise of Allah for creating the heavens and the earth and making darkness and light, and its subject throughout is the oneness of Allah: who He is, what He has made, and why setting up partners beside Him is folly.

### Where and when it was revealed

There is no disagreement that the whole of Al-An'am was revealed in Makkah. Ibn 'Abbas said so, in the report of 'Ikrimah and 'Ata' from him, and 'Abdullah ibn az-Zubayr said the same, in the report of Khasif from Mujahid. The leading scholars of tafsir agree. Ibn 'Abbas added, in a report recorded by At-Tabarani, that all of it was revealed at night, accompanied by seventy thousand angels raising their voices in glorification of Allah. As-Suddi said that Murrah said that 'Abdullah said it was revealed in the company of seventy thousand angels. Mujahid, al-Kalbi and Qatadah said more or less the same: the whole surah came down at one time, except for a few verses.

### What the surah covers

The surah begins by praising Allah as Creator of the heavens and the earth and Maker of darkness and light, then turns to the disbelievers who set up equals to their Lord. It argues that the Being who created everything cannot need a partner, and it answers the many false notions of its day. The Magians (Majus) made light and darkness into two creators, Yazdan and Ahriman. The polytheists of Arabia worshipped stones and trees. The Arya Samajists took spirit and matter to be pre-existent and independent. The Christians, despite professing one God, took 'Isa (Jesus) and his blessed mother as partners and relied on the theory of Unity in Trinity. The surah refutes all of these by saying that Allah is the sole Creator and Maker of everything, so ascribing partners to His divinity makes no sense.

The heavens are mentioned in the plural and the earth in the singular. One reading, in al-Bahr al-Muhit, takes this to mean that the seven heavens differ from one another in form and attributes while the seven earths are alike, so they are counted as one. This is tied to the verse that says the earth is seven like the heavens (65:12). Darkness is named in the plural and light in the singular, because An-Nur, the light, is more honored: it stands for the one straight path, while the many darknesses stand for the many paths of error. Creation is expressed as "created" for the heavens and the earth but "made" for darkness and light, to show that darkness and light are not independent and self-existent things but contingents and attributes. Darkness is named first because it is basic to this world, light coming only where particulars are present.

The surah also sets out the terms appointed for human life: a term for death and another, known only to Allah, for the Hereafter. It reminds the reader that Allah knows what is concealed and what is revealed and what people earn. It speaks of Adam, created from clay, and of the nations who received scripture before and denied it. It warns those who take Allah's signs lightly, and it consoles the Prophet ﷺ with the pattern of prophetic rejection. It speaks of sleep and death as signs of Allah's power over souls, of how all turn to Allah alone in crisis, and of the gradual destruction of defiant nations. It tells the story of Ibrahim (Abraham) rejecting his father's idolatry and arguing from the observation of creation. It names the ten divine commandments, refutes those who deny revelation, and sets out what is lawful and unlawful to eat, including the rules about cattle. It closes with the gathering of jinn and humans on the Day of Judgment and the complete dedication of life to Allah.

Along the way it cites other verses to make its points: the heavens and the earth in (16:48) and (65:12), the straight path in (6:153), the taking of souls by night in (6:60), the knowledge of the Hour in (7:187) and (79:42-44), and Allah as God of heaven and earth in (43:84).

### Its virtues

Al-Asfra'ini said that this surah consists of all the principles and subsidiaries of tawhid (oneness of Allah). It was prefaced with "Al-Hamdulillah" to teach that all praise belongs to Allah, who needs no praise from anyone, and the creation of the heavens and the earth and of darkness and light is the proof of His being the Praised One. The system by which heaven and earth are governed is so perfect in its coordination and unitary nature that it proclaims aloud that its Creator and Organiser can be none other than the one and only God. The flawlessly regulated revolution of the earth and the coming of light and darkness and day and night are events beyond human comprehension, and they show that God does not need any assistant in His creation or in His control of what He has created.

### In short

- Al-An'am is a Makkan surah of one hundred and sixty-five verses about the oneness of Allah.
- It was revealed in Makkah, according to Ibn 'Abbas and others, all at one time and at night with seventy thousand angels.
- It argues from creation that Allah alone deserves worship, and answers the false beliefs of its day.
- It sets out the terms of human life and death, the laws of lawful and unlawful food, and the gathering of all on the Day of Judgment.
- Al-Asfra'ini called it a summary of all the principles and subsidiaries of tawhid.

1.text:
The surah opens by praising Allah for the very things that prove He alone deserves worship: He created the heavens and the earth and made darkness and light. The verse is doing two things at once. It is a eulogy, describing Allah in the most beautiful terms, and it is an argument, because the One who made everything cannot need a partner. "All praise is for Allah Who created the heavens and the earth and made darkness and light. Yet the disbelievers set up equals to their Lord in worship." The last clause is the charge: in spite of all this creation, some of Allah's servants disbelieve in Him and hold others as partners and rivals with Him. Some of them even claimed a wife and a son for Allah, hallowed be He far above what they attribute to Him.

### Phrase by phrase

**"All praise is for Allah"** is Al-Hamdulillah. All praise belongs to Allah. The purpose of opening with it is to teach that Allah needs no praise from anyone. Whether or not anyone praises Him, He is the Praised One. This is in terms of His own intrinsic perfection. By Himself He is the Praised One. One of the great ones of the religion said, "Who is worthy of praise other than He whose power created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light?" The system by which heaven and earth are governed is so perfect in its coordination and unitary nature that it proclaims aloud that its Creator and Organiser can be none other than the one and only God.

**"Who created the heavens and the earth"** uses the word khalaqa. The heavens are named in the plural and the earth in the singular. One reading, in al-Bahr al-Muhit, takes this to mean that the seven heavens differ from one another in form and attributes while the seven earths are alike, so they are counted as one. This is tied to the verse that says the earth is seven like the heavens (65:12). Allah created the heavens and the earth as a dwelling for His servants, and the flawlessly regulated revolution of the earth around the sun, bringing light and darkness and day and night, is beyond human comprehension. The same system shows that God is so great that He does not need any assistant in His creation or in His control of what He has created.

**"and made darkness and light"** uses the word ja'ala. Darkness is named in the plural and light in the singular, because An-Nur, the light, is more honored. Light stands for the correct way and the straight path, and that is one. The many darknesses stand for the many paths of error, and their number runs in thousands. The cross references are to the verse that says "To the right and to the lefts" (16:48) and to the verse near the end of this surah that says "verily, this is my straight path, so follow it, and follow no other ways, for they will separate you away from His way" (6:153). The origination of the heavens and the earth is expressed through "created," while that of darkness and light is expressed through "made," to show that darkness and light are not independent and self-existent like the heavens and the earth. They are contingents and attributes. Darkness is named first because it is basic to this world, while light is associated with particulars: when they are there, there is light, and when they are not, there is darkness.

One reading gives the days of creation: the heavens in two days, Sunday and Monday, and the earth in two days, Tuesday and Wednesday, with darkness and light read as faith and disbelief, or as night and day.

**"Yet the disbelievers set up equals to their Lord in worship"** is the charge. In spite of all this, some of Allah's servants disbelieve in Him and hold others as partners and rivals with Him. Some of them claimed a wife and a son for Allah. The verse refutes every form of this. The Magians (Majus) believe in two creators. They are Yazdan and Ahriman. They identify them with light and darkness. The polytheists in India take an incredibly high number of gods. They take them as partners in the divinity of God. The Arya Samajists acknowledge the oneness of God. Despite that, they take spirit and matter to be infinitely pre-existent. They take them to be independent of the power and creation of God. The Christians profess one God. Despite that, they took 'Isa (Jesus) and his blessed mother as partners. They relied on the theory of Unity in Trinity. As for the disbelievers and polytheists of Arabia, they treated every piece of rock on a hill as good enough. It could become an object of worship. By saying that Allah is the Creator of the heavens and the earth and the Maker of darkness and light, all such false notions are refuted: when He is the sole Creator and Maker of everything, ascribing partners to His divinity makes no sense.

### Why is darkness named in the plural and light in the singular?

Because An-Nur, the light, is more honored, and because light stands for the one straight path while the darknesses stand for the many paths of error. The straight path is single, but the ways that lead away from it are countless.

### The mystical reading of the verse

Praise belongs to God. He begins by lauding Himself. He praises Himself with His own beginningless laudation. He reports His own self-sufficient brilliance. He reports His own unitary elevation. This is praise of the tremendous Lord. He is the wise Enactor. He is subsistent through His own subsistence. He is transcendent through His own attributes. He is magnificent through His own magnificence. His elevation is everlasting. His brilliance is self-standing. His existence is unitary. His being is self-sufficient. His face is majestic. His power is perfect. Glory be to Him. God is the One. He is the All-Subjugating (39:4). He is exalted. He is the all-compeller. He is great. He is transcendent. One of the great ones of the religion and leaders of the Tariqah said, "Who is worthy of praise other than He whose power created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light?" As the Shaykh Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli states in his commentary on surat al-Kahf, Q. 181, praise may be informative or eulogy or both. One may say that the straight path is one, and the path of error is many. Who else is fitting to be praised for purity and named for greatness? He created heaven and earth. He created day and night. He set up heaven like a roof. He adorned earth like a cradle. He readied the day for your livelihood. He made the night your time of rest.

Heaven can also be read as an allusion to the heaven of recognition. That heaven is the hearts of the recognizers. Earth can be read as an allusion to the earth of service. That earth is the souls of the worshipers. He decorated heaven with the form of the stars. He adorned it with sun and moon. He made it the gazing place of the earth-dwellers. In the same way, He adorned the heaven of recognition with the sun of knowledge. He adorned it with the moon of tawhid (oneness of Allah). He adorned it with the stars of thoughts. Then He made it the gazing place of the heaven-dwellers. Whenever the satans aim to listen stealthily, they are subjugated. They are subjugated from the heaven of exaltedness by the stoning of stars. This is why the Exalted Lord said, "We have made them stonings for the satans" (67:5). Whenever Satan aims to instill disquiet, a lightning flashes. It flashes in the heart of the faithful servant from the heaven of recognition. It burns Satan. This is why He says, "Surely the godwary, when a visitation from..." (7:201). On the expanse of the earth there are seven seas. In them are benefits and livelihood for creatures.

### In short

- The surah opens by praising Allah as Creator of the heavens and the earth and Maker of darkness and light.
- The plural darknesses and singular light mean that the straight path is one while the paths of error are many.
- Darkness and light are made, not created, because they are attributes and contingents, not independent things.
- The verse refutes every form of associating partners with Allah.
- Even so, the disbelievers set up equals to their Lord in worship.

2.text:
The verse turns from the great universe to the small one: the human being. "He is the One Who created you from clay, then appointed a term for your death and another known only to Him for your resurrection, yet you continue to doubt." The argument is that the One who made you from clay and gave you life can raise you again, so doubting the resurrection is unreasonable. This is a proof of the oneness of Allah. The people of Makkah were the ones addressed. The verse also names the two ends of human life: death, which is personal, and the Day of Resurrection, which is collective and known only to Allah.

### Phrase by phrase

**"He is the One Who created you from clay"** refers to the father of mankind, Adam, from whom mankind originated, multiplied in numbers, and spread about, east and west. The clay is the moist substance from which common human food comes, and from food the sperm, and from the sperm the creation of the human being. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said that he heard from the Prophet ﷺ that Allah created Adam from a particular blend of clay that included the essential ingredients of the whole earth, and that is why the children of Adam differ in color, shape, morals, and habits: some black, some white, some red, some hard, some soft, some good-natured, some evil-tempered. This is a report with good authority, from Ibn 'Adiyy through Mazhari. Adam was two things. Clay and spirituality. His clay pertained to the World of the Creation. His spirituality pertained to the World of the Command. "He fermented Adam's clay in His hand" pertains to creation, and "I have blown into him of My spirit" (15:29) pertains to the command. "Surely God chose Adam" (3:33) pertains to the beauty of the command. "Adam disobeyed" (20:121) pertains to the taint of creation. In Adam there were both a rose garden and a field of clay. Thus the clay was the place of roses. Every rose, however, has a thorn. A rose like the bosom friend Abraham (Ibrahim) had a thorn like the rebellious Nimrod. A rose like Moses (Musa) had thorns like Pharaoh and Haman. A rose like Jesus ('Isa) had thorns. They were like those impure Jews. A rose like Muhammad ﷺ the Arab had a thorn. It was like Abu Jahl the wretched. Who knows the secret of Adam's innate disposition? Indeed, who recognizes it? Who recognizes Adam's good fortune and rank? No eagle of anyone's mind has alighted on the branch of the tree of Adam's good fortune. No eye of anyone's insight has perceived the beauty of the sun of Adam's limpidness. He was at rest. He was in the highest paradises. He supposed that the same tent of safety would be pitched for him endlessly. Then he was addressed. It was by the side of the Compeller. It was by the court of the Exalted. "What, one who is reared amidst ornaments?" (43:18). O Adam, We want to make a man of you. You have become satisfied with color and scent. You are like pretty brides. How long will you sit like a woman? You hope for color and scent. Fix your aspiration on the road. Set out like a man. [DS 205] O Adam, pull your hands back from the neck of Eve. You must use your hands. Use them for the neck of passion's crocodile. You must become the drinking companion of the Shariah's lion. Pull back from the attributes of being. Travel with the feet of discipline. Travel with the boots of blame. Go into the open horizons of poverty. Go, sit on the dust-pile. Be content with a piece of bread. Be content with ragged clothes. Be content with ruins. So that you may become a man. Throw away life. Travel the road. Live upright. Be a man. Then you will subsist. You will subsist when you empty your skirt of these ruins.

**"then appointed a term for your death"** is the personal end of a human being. Allah fixed a period for your stay in the life of the world. Reaching the completion of this term is death. Human beings do not know their own term, but the angels do, and human beings know death in a way, because the children of Adam die all around, everywhere, all the time. The world's age is limited. Here life cannot be devoid of grief. Here unpleasantness goes along with pleasantness. Evil cannot be separated from goodness. Goodness cannot be separated from evil. In such circumstances, man is unable to understand something. How can the eternal world of the Hereafter, which will be free from grief (35:34), come into existence? If the other world is to be created from the matter of this world, it has to be conceded. This world in itself lacks the capacity. It cannot bring into existence a world of total perfection. But the very existence of the one who raises the issue is the answer. The body of a human being is wholly made of earth elements, yet it has unique properties, none of which is found in the earth. Man hears. He speaks. He thinks. He performs wonderful acts. The earth with which he is made is not capable. It cannot perform these acts. From earthen elements a non-earthly creature has wondrously emerged. If a living and active man comes into existence from earth, and fragrant flowers and luscious fruits emerge from earth, then why cannot a more perfect world emerge from our present world?

**"and another known only to Him for your resurrection"** is the combined end of the entire humankind along with all the cosmic servants waiting on them, which is known as the Qiyamah (the Day of Doom). This term is fixed and known to Allah alone. The full knowledge of it has not been given to any angel or human being. The knowledge thereof is with the Lord. None can reveal its time but He (7:187). They ask about the Hour, when will be its appointed time? You have no knowledge to say anything about it. To the Lord belongs the term thereof (79:42-44). He is the One who takes your souls by night. This is when you are asleep. He has knowledge of all that you have done by day. Then He raises you up again. A term appointed be fulfilled (6:60).

**"yet you continue to doubt"** is the charge. Using the personal death of a human being as proof of the general and collective death of the whole world system, that is, the Qiyamah, is something very natural and logical. Therefore, no doubt remains about the coming of the Qiyamah. The message of God and the Hereafter is accompanied by clear signs. These establish it as a true call from the Almighty. It is on the lines of nature. That nature is the system of God's eternal world. It is supported by arguments. These cannot be countered by anybody. It is backed by a preacher of God's word. His seriousness and sincerity are above doubt. It has repeatedly survived the destructive plans of its opponents. This is despite their superior power. All of these are clear indications. They show that it is based on truth. In spite of all this, man does not believe in it. He is not willing to support it. The reason is that all these proofs always appear through a veil. It is a veil of cause and effect. When these signs come to a man's attention, he attributes them to certain causes. He pays no heed to them. He does not become inclined to accept their validity. Instead of accepting the call, he says something else. Had this call been on behalf of God, then God and His angels would have been visible. They would be visible to the naked eye. But this idea is absolutely meaningless. When God and His angels appear in all their glory, it will be the time for the final rendering of accounts. It will not be the time for giving a call of Truth. It will not be the time for preaching about the greatness of God.

### Why the verse moves from the universe to the human being

The first verse speaks of the big universe. The whole wide world was created and made by Allah. The second verse speaks of the small universe. The human being was also created by Allah. Then, to shake human beings out of their negligence, a further point is made. Every human being has a particular age. After that age, death is certain. This is a constant fact of life. Human beings observe it all the time. The words about the fixed term carry an instruction. Using personal death as proof of the general death of the whole world system is natural and logical. So no doubt remains about the coming of the Qiyamah. The Qiyamah is the much publicized but least believed Apocalypse of the West. Towards the end of the verse, the text wonders why people keep doubting the coming of the Qiyamah. It stands proved so clearly.

### In short

- Allah created the human being from clay, through Adam, and appointed a term for death and a term for resurrection known only to Him.
- The personal death of a human being is proof of the collective end of the world.
- The body is made of earth yet has properties the earth does not have, so a more perfect world can emerge from this one.
- The signs of the Hereafter are clear, but people attribute them to causes and keep doubting.
- Adam was both clay and spirit, and every rose has its thorn.

3.text:
The third verse draws the consequence from the first two. "He is the Only True God in the heavens and the earth. He knows whatever you conceal and whatever you reveal, and knows whatever you do." Because He created everything and appointed the terms of life and death, He alone is worthy of worship in the heavens and on the earth, and nothing is hidden from Him.

### Phrase by phrase

**"He is the Only True God in the heavens and the earth"** means that He is the One called Allah throughout the heavens and the earth: the One who is worshipped. He is singled out. His divinity is believed in by the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth. They call Him Allah and supplicate to Him in fear and hope, except those who disbelieve among the jinn and mankind. In another verse, "It is He Who is God in the heavens and the earth" (43:84), meaning He is the God of those in heaven and those on earth. He is the One worthy of worship in the heavens and in the earth, and He will judge people about their intentions, statements, and actions.

**"He knows whatever you conceal and whatever you reveal"** means He knows what you keep hidden in your breasts just as He knows what you make public. He knows all affairs, public and secret. Nothing is hidden from Him, whether in the heart or in speech.

**"and knows whatever you do"** means all the good and bad deeds that you perform. He knows what you earn.

### The inner reading

One can say that He is in heaven through Essence. He is everywhere through knowledge. He is in the spirit through companionship. He is in the soul through proximity. The soul comes to nothing in Him. He takes the place of the spirit that comes to nothing in Him. He is in finding where found. He is in recognition where recognized. Reports do not spoil the Haqiqah (reality). The Haqiqah does not nullify the reports. Say "He sat" (7:54). He is upon the Throne through sitting. Recite "He is with you" (57:4). He is with you wherever you are. He does not take up place through need. He displays places through mercy. He built the Throne for the God-seekers. The God-recognizers have no need of it. Should a God-recognizer take one breath without Him, he would have bound the sash of unbelief. O boast of my tongue in the two worlds. Delight of my spirit in tomorrow's vision. My occupation in the two worlds. Remake my situation's occupation with Yourself. I have no spirit to scatter before the finding of You. I have no tongue to acknowledge Your favors. He who sees You is concealed in vision. He who seeks You is neither on earth nor in heaven.

### In short

- Allah alone is worthy of worship in the heavens and on the earth.
- He knows what is concealed, what is revealed, and what people do.
- The verse draws the consequence from creation and from the appointed terms of life and death.
- Nothing is hidden from Him, in heart or in deed.

4.text:
The verse is a complaint against the stubbornness of the disbelievers. "Whenever a sign comes to them from their Lord, they turn away from it." No proof or miracle from their Lord comes to the idolaters except that they ignore it without paying any attention. Clear evidences and proofs of the oneness of Allah have now come to them. Miracles proving the truthfulness of the messengers have now come to them. Yet despite this they turned away. They paid no attention to these signs and miracles.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Whenever a sign comes to them from their Lord"** means any proof, miracle, or revelation from the signs of Allah. The people of Makkah were shown signs such as the eclipse of the sun, the splitting of the moon, and the stars, and each time they disbelieved in the sign.

**"they turn away from it"** means they do not contemplate these signs or care about them. Despite the many clear proofs and open signs of the oneness of Allah, the dissenters and rejectionists take a way of their own and turn their faces away from whatever sign is shown to them for their guidance, without ever paying the least attention to it.

### In short

- Every sign from Allah is met by the disbelievers with turning away.
- They ignore clear proofs of the oneness of Allah and of the messengers' truthfulness.
- Their rejection is stubborn and deliberate, not a lack of evidence.

5.text:
The verse presses the charge further. "They have indeed rejected the truth when it came to them, so they will soon face the consequences of their ridicule." The word Al-Haqq (the truth) here could mean the Qur'an, and it could mean the blessed person of the Prophet ﷺ himself, for both came to the people of Makkah and both were rejected. Say to them that the respite is now.

### Phrase by phrase

**"They have indeed rejected the truth when it came to them"** refers to the Qur'an and to the Prophet ﷺ. His whole life was lived among these Arab tribes. He grew up from a child into a young man. From his youth into his later years, right before their eyes. They knew fully well that he had remained absolutely untaught by any human teacher, so much so that he could not write even his name by himself. The whole of Arabia knew him by his appellation of Ummi (unlettered, unschooled). For forty years this was him amongst them. He never demonstrated any marked interest in poetry. Poetry was a traditional distinction of the age. He had no aptitude for formal education. He had no aptitude for learning. After he completed his forty years, there came a sudden change. An instant flowering of the unimaginable. His blessed tongue became such a fountainhead. It was a fountainhead of insights and realities. It was a fountainhead of learning and arts. It went on to disarm the best minds of the world. He challenged every eloquent and learned master of words in Arabia. They were to match the Word he brought. But his antagonists did not have the courage. They would not have hesitated to sacrifice anything they had. Life, wealth, honour, children, family, anything, anytime, just to defeat him. Yet they did not produce even one verse like a verse of the Qur'an. Thus the very presence of the Prophet ﷺ and the Glorious Qur'an was a great sign of irrefutable legitimacy. In addition to that, there were thousands of miracles and open signs that came to pass at his blessed hands and that cannot be denied by any sane person. But those people belied all such signs totally.

**"so they will soon face the consequences of their ridicule"** is the threat. Right now these people, heedless of their fate, mock the miracles and commandments of Allah brought by the Prophet ﷺ and the all-true message that there is a Qiyamah (Doomsday) and an Akhirah (Hereafter). But very soon will come the time. All these realities will be before their eyes. There will be a Qiyamah in fact. There will be a reckoning. Everyone will have to account for one's faith and deed. Everyone shall get the reward or punishment for what he or she has done. But believing and confessing at that time will not work. That will be no day of deeds. Rather, that day will be the day of Retribution. The time to think is now. Allah has given the respite. It is a God-sent piece of luck. Act now. It is by having faith alone that you will succeed. You will succeed in this world. You will succeed in the lasting world to come.

One reading specifies the punishment. It is the news of their derision. It is the punishment of their derision. This happened on the Day of Badr. It happened on the Day of Uhud. It happened on the Day of the Confederates.

### Why the established of this world mock the truth

Those who have firmly established themselves in this world, having accumulated many material goods, and who see the manifestations of their own greatness and popularity around them, are always liable to misunderstanding. They look down upon the things Allah has gathered around the caller of truth as compared to the things around them. This overweening confidence increases to such an extent that they even become unafraid of Allah. They make fun of the warning given by the missionary of truth. If their arrogance continued, their material achievements would not be able to save them. They would not be saved from Allah's scourge. Their treatment of the caller as a non-entity makes his warnings also insignificant. Even historic instances of Allah having destroyed materially well-set-up people, as if their lives were of no value whatsoever, fail to teach them a lesson. Events happen again and again. One set of people faces decline. Another set rises. This shows something else. The rule of crime and punishment is prevalent here. However, man does not learn a lesson from this. The succeeding generations repeat those very same actions. Their predecessors indulged in them. Due to those actions they were destroyed.

### In short

- The disbelievers rejected the truth, the Qur'an and the Prophet ﷺ, when it came to them.
- The Prophet's ﷺ unlettered upbringing and sudden flowering of revelation was itself a sign.
- They will soon face the consequences of their ridicule on the Day of Judgment.
- Believing after the punishment arrives will not help.
- Those established in this world mock the truth because of their overweening confidence.

6.text:
The verse asks the disbelievers to look at history. "Have they not seen how many disbelieving peoples We destroyed before them? We had made them more established in the land than you. We sent down abundant rain for them and made rivers flow at their feet. Then We destroyed them for their sins and replaced them with other peoples." The point is that power and prosperity do not protect a people from Allah's punishment when they deny the truth.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Have they not seen how many disbelieving peoples We destroyed before them"** means, have they not considered the communities that Allah destroyed before them? The word qarn is used for a group of people. They are collectively present at a given time and period. It is also used to denote a long period of time. That period could be, depending on different interpretations, between ten and one hundred years. Some events and narrations support the position that this word is used for one hundred years. The Prophet ﷺ told 'Abdullah ibn Busr al-Ma'ziniyy that he would live for one qarn, and when the Prophet ﷺ prayed for a certain child that he might live for a whole qarn, he did live for a full one hundred years. The majority of scholars take the famous hadith, still recited as part of the khutbah of Jumu'ah all over the world, to mean exactly this, that every qarn is one hundred years. The people of Makkah had not seen these generations with their own eyes, for "seen" here means to ponder about them.

**"We had made them more established in the land than you"** means that Allah had established those past peoples on the earth with more stability and power than the people of Makkah. The people of Makkah did not have the power of the legendary people of 'Ad and Thamud, nor the affluence of the people of Syria and Yemen. Those earlier peoples had more wealth, children, buildings, abundant provision, riches, and soldiers.

**"We sent down abundant rain for them and made rivers flow at their feet"** means rain that comes often, and springs that were plentiful, so that they were deceived by their prosperity. Allah poured out rain from the sky in abundance and made the rivers flow under them, beneath their fields, plantations, and trees.

**"Then We destroyed them for their sins"** means the mistakes and errors they committed, their denial of the prophets and their disobedience to divine injunctions. All that majesty of power and wealth was rendered futile against the punishment of Allah, which annihilated them totally.

**"and replaced them with other peoples"** means that after those generations perished and became legends and stories, Allah created other generations in their place, as if nothing had happened there and no one was missing from the scene. This spectacle of divine power and wisdom is observable in every time and period, when thousands die every day but no vacuum is left anywhere. One reflects on the plains of 'Arafat with a million men and women spread around, and realizes that only seventy or eighty years earlier none among that whole assembly existed, while on that same place nearly that many other human beings were present, no trace of whom exists today. Praised be Allah, the best of creators.

### The lesson of history

Events of the past are documents full of chastening lessons. If seen to find wisdom, they would prove more effective than a thousand sermons. So still valid is the saying of the sage. The world is the best book. Time is the best teacher. That is why wisdom-based historical anecdotes form a good part of the Qur'an. Speaking generally, people have not given world history any serious role. They have not used it in conducting lives properly. Rather than benefiting from it, they made it into an intellectual pastime. It would either help to sleep. Or it would while away spare time. Perhaps it is for this reason that the Qur'an has taken the essence of history as a server of warning and a dispenser of good counsel. The Qur'an has not taken up historical events as ongoing events in their own right. Instead, it places part of the narrative as relevant to the given subject and setting of the message in the text, and then on another occasion, another place, it describes another part of the story as relevant there. A report or story is not an end in itself. The purpose is to identify the outcome of the report and the practical implication of the event, so one should be concerned with what is necessary for the objective in sight, move ahead, and survey his circumstances in that light. Learn that vital lesson from what has gone before and thereby correct oneself.

For the people of Makkah, the need of the hour was to learn a lesson. They should learn from what happened to the peoples of the past. They should turn towards an examination of their doings. They should think where they are going to end up. This is by opposing the truth. Allah advises and warns the disbelievers. They should avoid the torments and afflictions of this life. These are similar to what befell their likes from previous nations. You are not more beloved to Allah than those earlier nations. But the Messenger you defied holds a higher place with Allah. It is higher than the Messengers they defied. Thus you are more liable than them to receive torment. This is so if it was not for Allah's mercy and kindness.

### In short

- Allah destroyed many peoples before the disbelievers of Makkah, though they were more established and prosperous.
- Their destruction came because of their sins, their denial of the prophets.
- Allah then raised up other peoples in their place.
- Power and prosperity do not protect from Allah's punishment.
- History is a warning, not a pastime, and the people of Makkah are more liable to torment than those before them.

7.text:
The verse answers a stubborn demand. "Had We sent down to you, O Prophet, a revelation in writing and they were to touch it with their own hands, the disbelievers would still have said, 'This is nothing but pure magic!'" The point is that the disbelievers' rejection is not a matter of evidence. Even if they saw the revelation descend and touched it with their own hands, they would still call it magic. Their words come from malice and hostility, not from a lack of proof.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Had We sent down to you a revelation in writing"** refers to a book sent down from heaven, as 'Abdullah ibn Umayyah al-Makhzumi and his friends demanded. Al-Kalbi said that the idolaters of Makkah said something. O Muhammad, by Allah we will not believe until you bring us a book from Allah. It must come along with four angels with it. Al-Walibi reported Ibn 'Abbas saying: We brought doubts around them. Strange are the ways of fate, for this very gentleman embraced Islam later on and received his shahadah (martyrdom) in the Battle of Ta'if. Gabriel (Jibril) al-Amin came to the Prophet ﷺ in the shape of a human being. They asked for a book from Allah along with four angels bearing witness that it was from Allah and that Muhammad ﷺ was His messenger. Even if such a book were sent, they would not accept it.

**"and they were to touch it with their own hands"** means they could see it for themselves and even physically touch it, so that they would know they were not day-dreaming and that it was a reality. Touch is more effective than sight in removing doubt. Yet even this would not move them.

**"the disbelievers would still have said, 'This is nothing but pure magic!'"** is the charge. They would still say it is nothing but obvious magic, a clear lie. This is because what they say comes from malice and hostility. They are a kind of people who would not stop at what they demanded. Even if they were presented with far clearer proofs of their Prophet's veracity, they would still not believe.

### Why the disbelievers reject even clear proof

The reason a man goes astray in this world is that here he has complete freedom. He can reject the truth. He even has the opportunity to give fine justifications. These are for erroneous thoughts, words, and deeds. Man enjoys full freedom in this world of trial. He can accept the truth. He can reject the truth. He does as he pleases. Should the preacher of God's word appear in the shape of an ordinary man, the reason given for ignoring him could be this. So be it. His effectiveness hinges on a talent for leadership. It has nothing to do with truth. It has nothing to do with righteousness. Similarly, if a book complete in every detail comes down from the sky, he will say, "This is mere magic." He says this to justify his rejection of it. The people of Makkah used to ask for such proofs. But they were not making their demands out of any good intention. They were not likely to accept the truth even if their demands were met.

This is similar to Allah's description of the disbelievers' defiance of facts and truth: "And even if We opened to them a gate from the heaven and they were to continue ascending thereto. They would surely say: Our eyes have been as if dazzled. Nay, we are a people bewitched" (15:14-15), and "And if they were to see a piece of the heaven falling down, they would say, Clouds gathered in heaps!" (52:44).

### Comfort for the Prophet

The verse comforts the Prophet ﷺ concerning the denial of him by his people. The demands of his antagonists were not put forward for any useful purpose, nor did they want to follow the truth. They were a kind of people who would not stop at what they demanded. So let this concern bring no sorrow to his heart. His task is to convey the commandments of Allah. When he feels he has done that, let his heart be at rest. Whether someone is affected by the message or not is not for him to worry about. It is not a part of his duty as a Messenger of Allah.

### In short

- Even a written revelation from heaven, touched by their own hands, would not move the disbelievers.
- Their rejection comes from malice and hostility, not from a lack of evidence.
- A man in this world of trial has freedom to reject the truth and to justify his rejection.
- The verse comforts the Prophet ﷺ: his duty is to convey, not to force acceptance.

8.text:
The verse answers another demand. "They say, 'Why has no visible angel come with him?' Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have certainly been settled at once, and they would have never been given more time to repent." The disbelievers asked for an angel to testify that the book was from Allah and that Muhammad ﷺ was His messenger. The answer is that if such an angel were sent, the matter would be judged at once, and no respite would be granted to them.

### Phrase by phrase

**"They say, 'Why has no visible angel come with him?'"** refers to the demand of 'Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah, accompanied by Nadr ibn al-Harith and Nawfal ibn Khalid. Ibn Umayyah al-Makhzumi was the one who demanded a book from heaven. Abi Umaiyyah came with Nadr ibn al-Harith. Al-Walibi reported Ibn 'Abbas saying: We brought doubts around them. They said they would believe only if Allah sent down an angel with Muhammad ﷺ who would speak to them and bear witness that he was a messenger.

**"Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have certainly been settled at once"** means that if We sent the angel they demanded, then these people, who are not the kind who would accept truth, would still act contrary and hostile even after having seen the miracle. Then the Divine command to have them destroyed would stand activated. The angel would come down to punish them and take away their souls.

**"and they would have never been given more time to repent"** means they would be given no respite after that happens. They would not be allowed any delay. The fact of not showing the miracle demanded by them spells out real good for them, without which they would be nowhere. This is because the Divine law is this. Should a people ask their prophet to show a miracle of their choice, and as a result of their demand such a miracle is shown by the power and will of Allah, then, should they remain reluctant even then to believe and accept faith any longer, they are destroyed. They are destroyed by a mass general punishment.

### The mercy in withholding the miracle

These particular people of Makkah were really not making their demands as based on any good intentions, which may have at least given some hope of their accepting the truth. Therefore, the fact that the miracle was withheld is a mercy for them. We send not the angels down except with the truth, and in that case they would have no respite (15:8). On the Day they will see the angels, no glad tidings will there be for the criminals that day (25:22).

### In short

- The disbelievers demanded an angel to testify for the Prophet ﷺ.
- If an angel were sent, the matter would be judged at once and they would be destroyed.
- Withholding the miracle is a mercy, since they would not accept the truth anyway.
- The Divine law destroys those who demand a miracle and then still refuse to believe.

9.text:
The verse gives a second answer. "And if We had sent an angel, We would have certainly made it assume the form of a man, leaving them more confused than they already are." People asking such questions are strange. There are only two ways an angel can come down. If an angel comes as he is, in his form and state of being, no human being can stand before his real awe. The sight is too much. In fact, he is more likely to die. He would die at the never imagined sight. The second form in which the angel could come down is different. is that the angel comes in human shape and form, as Jibril (Gabriel) al-Amin came to the Prophet ﷺ several times in the shape of a human being. In this situation too, the questioner will have the same objection against this angel as he has against the Prophet ﷺ, because he would take him to be nothing but human.

### Phrase by phrase

**"And if We had sent an angel"** means if We appointed an angel as Our messenger. Al-Walibi reported Ibn 'Abbas saying: We brought doubts around them. Abi Umaiyyah demanded a book from heaven.

**"We would have certainly made it assume the form of a man"** means We would have made him in the form of a man. So that they could listen and learn from him. They would not be able to learn from an angel in the original form that Allah created him. They would be able to look at him. They would benefit from his teachings.

**"leaving them more confused than they already are"** means We would have confused them over their confusion. They would be confused about him, just as they are confused about the Prophet ﷺ. They would say, "This is but a mere mortal like the rest of you." Say: "If there were on the earth, angels walking about in peace and security, We should certainly have sent down for them from the heaven an angel as a Messenger" (17:95).

### The mercy of human messengers

It is a mercy from Allah to His creation. He sends every type of creation. Messengers come from among their kind. So that they are able to call their people to Allah. And their people are able to talk to them. They can ask them. They can benefit from them. Indeed Allah conferred a great favor on the believers. He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves. He recited unto them His verses. He purified them (3:164). Ad-Dahhak said that Ibn 'Abbas said about this verse: "If an angel was sent to them, he would come in the shape of a man. This is because they will not be able to look at the angel due to light."

### In short

- An angel sent down would have to appear as a man, or the people could not bear it.
- Either way, the disbelievers would still object and be confused.
- Sending human messengers is a mercy, so people can talk to them and benefit.
- The verse removes the disbelievers' excuse for rejecting the Prophet ﷺ.

10.text:
The verse consoles the Prophet ﷺ. "Other messengers had already been ridiculed before you, O Prophet, but those who mocked them were overtaken by what they used to ridicule." This attitude of mockery and injury directed against him by his people is not something particular to him. It happened to others too. Other prophets and messengers before him had to face similar heart-breaking experiences. Yet they did not lose hope. Finally, what happened was that those who used to mock were overtaken. They were overtaken by the punishment which they mocked at.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Other messengers had already been ridiculed before you"** means that communities in the past also poked fun at their messengers. Al-Walibi reported Ibn 'Abbas saying: We brought doubts around them. Abi Umaiyyah demanded a book from heaven. Messengers of Allah have been derided before you, as your people are deriding you now. This is meant as a consolation for the Prophet ﷺ.

**"but those who mocked them were overtaken by what they used to ridicule"** means that the punishment, which they used to deny and mock when they were warned about it, surrounded them. Those who scoffed at them were encompassed by that which they mocked. Those who mock you will be encompassed likewise.

### In short

- Mockery of messengers is not new. It happened to prophets before.
- Those who mocked were overtaken by the very punishment they ridiculed.
- The verse comforts the Prophet ﷺ and promises a good end for the believers.

11.text:
The verse closes the passage with a command. "Say, 'Travel throughout the land and see the fate of the deniers.'" The Prophet ﷺ is told to say to these people who deny and mock him: travel on earth. Then think about what happened. Think about those who disbelieved in Allah's messengers. Allah's punishment fell upon them after they were in a position of strength and power. Contemplate about yourselves. Think about the afflictions Allah struck the previous nations with. Those nations defied His Messengers. They denied them. Allah sent torment, afflictions, and punishment on them in this life. He sent the painful torment in the Hereafter. He saved His Messengers and believing servants.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Say"** is the command to the Prophet ﷺ to address the disbelievers. Al-Walibi reported Ibn 'Abbas saying: We brought doubts around them. Abi Umaiyyah demanded a book from heaven. The people of Makkah were the ones addressed.

**"Travel throughout the land"** means go and see, travel in the land and reflect.

**"and see the fate of the deniers"** means see the nature of the consequence for the deniers of the messengers, how they were destroyed through chastisement. Perhaps they will take heed.

### In short

- The Prophet ﷺ is commanded to tell the disbelievers to travel and see.
- The fate of past deniers is a warning for the present.
- Allah saved His messengers and believers while punishing the deniers.

12.text:
The verse asks and answers a question, then promises the gathering. "Ask them, O Prophet, 'To whom belongs everything in the heavens and the earth?' Say, 'To Allah!' He has taken upon Himself to be Merciful. He will certainly gather all of you together for the Day of Judgment, about which there is no doubt. But those who have ruined themselves will never believe." The disbelievers of Makkah already accepted that Allah is the Master of the heavens and the earth and everything they contain. The verse uses that accepted fact to press the point: if He is the Master, then He will gather everyone on the Day of Resurrection, and those who have brought loss to themselves by disbelief will not believe.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Ask them, O Prophet, 'To whom belongs everything in the heavens and the earth?'"** is the question put to the disbelievers. This is the opening of the passage. The disbelievers of Makkah already accepted that Allah is the Master. Tawhid (oneness of Allah) is the theme. "Do you order me to worship other than Allah, O you fools?" (39:64). "I created not the Jinn and humans except that they should worship Me" (51:56). The number 12 marks this verse. Say to them: travel and see. The answer is not waited for, because the disbelievers of Makkah were no deniers of the fact that Allah Almighty is the Master of the heavens and the earth and everything they contain, even though they were involved in shirk and idolatry.

**"Say, 'To Allah!'"** is the answer given through the Prophet ﷺ. To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. Their total control belongs to Allah.

**"He has taken upon Himself to be Merciful"** means that Allah has prescribed mercy for Himself, out of grace for His servants. He will not rush to punish them. It is recorded in the Two Sahihs that Abu Hurayrah said that the Prophet ﷺ said: "When Allah created the creation, He wrote in a Book that He has with Him above the Throne: 'My mercy overcomes My anger.'" Abu Hurayrah narrated that a man from Al-Ansar from the area of Quba' invited the Prophet ﷺ to eat some food. When the Prophet ﷺ ate and washed his hands, he said: "All praise is due to Allah. He feeds but is never fed. He bestowed bounty unto us. He gave us guidance. He fed us. He gave us something to drink. He covered our nakedness. For every favor He has given us. All praise is due to Allah alone. Indeed, praise that should not be neglected, my Lord. So be it. All the while affirming that we will never be able to duly thank Him. Indeed. Nor be appreciative enough of Him. Nor be free of needing Him." Sayyidna Abu Hurairah reported this in the Sahih of Muslim.

**"He will certainly gather all of you together for the Day of Judgment"** means that Allah will gather everyone, from the beginning to the end, on the Day of Qiyamah. Muhammad ﷺ is the one who conveys this. You Yourself are the Master. The unseen is known to Him. The word "towards" can also mean to gather in the graves. In that case it means that human beings will be kept being gathered into their resting places. This is unto the Day of Qiyamah. Then they will be raised back to life. The Day of Resurrection is a known Day, about which there is no doubt. Allah swore by His Most Honored Self that He will gather His servants for an appointed meeting of a known Day (56:50).

**"about which there is no doubt"** is the assurance for the believing servants. As for those who deny and refuse, they are in confusion and disarray.

**"But those who have ruined themselves will never believe"** means that those who have brought loss to themselves by disbelief will not believe and rescue their souls from loss. The deprivation of the disbelievers from the universal mercy of Allah mentioned earlier was caused by their own deeds. They did not take to the way which brings mercy. That is, the way of belief and faith.

### The mystical reading

The mystical reading asks whether anyone truly dwells in the house, and answers that God in His lordship is enough. It says that all is from God to God. It says that God struck the coin of mercy before creating anything, so that His mercy takes precedence over His wrath. On the Day of Mustering, the Messenger will intercede for the disobedient, asking that they be clothed in the shirt of mercy, citing God's own words: "We sent thee only as a mercy to the worlds" (21:107) and "O My servants who have been immoderate against yourselves, despair not of God's mercy" (39:53). From the Court of Majesty will come the call that the work of the community is one of three: people of faith, recognizers, or the disobedient, and to each will be given paradise or mercy and forgiveness. "Surely I am God; there is no god but I" (20:14).

### In short

- Allah is the Master of everything in the heavens and the earth.
- He has prescribed mercy for Himself and will not rush to punish.
- He will gather everyone on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt.
- Those who ruin themselves by disbelief will not believe.
- The verse is a gentle summoning to faith, grounded in mercy.

13.text:
The verse extends the thought. "To Him belongs whatever exists in the day and night. And He is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing." Whatever rests hidden in the night and whatever moves about openly in the day are all His servants. They are His creation. They are all under His domination and control. He hears their statements. He knows their actions. He will judge by them.

### Phrase by phrase

**"To Him belongs whatever exists in the day and night"** means that all creatures in the heavens and earth are Allah's servants and creatures. They are all under His authority, power, and will. Indeed. There is no deity worthy of worship except Him. "Do you order me to worship other than Allah, O you fools?" (39:64). "I created not the Jinn and humans except that they should worship Me" (51:56). Say: the tawhid is clear. The word "sukun" could mean the state of being still or at rest, in which case the verse means that Allah is the Master of everything present in the night and the day. Or it could mean a combined state of stillness and movement, but what was mentioned here is the state of rest only, because movement, which stands in contrast to it, can be understood as being obvious enough.

**"And He is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing"** means that He hears the statements of His servants and knows their actions, secrets, and what they conceal.

### The mystical reading

The mystical reading says that the newly arriving things are God's as a kingdom, in God as manifestation, from God in appearance, and unto God in return. He is the Hearing of the moans of the yearners and the Knowing of the longing of the finders. Night is a general darkness and day a general brightness. Before the creation of the world there was neither night nor day. In paradise there is no sun, but all is day. Whatever is closer to God has a more complete light. 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "Surely there is no day or night with your Lord. He illuminates the heavens with the light of His face." The Lord of the Worlds created a tremendous angel, placing night in one of his fists and day in the other. By way of allusion, God is saying: "I placed the disk of the sun in the fist of the angel, but I did not give the hearts of My friends to anyone." The heart of the lovers is in the fist of the King. Mus'tafa said: "The hearts of the servants are between two fingers of the All-Merciful."

### In short

- Everything that rests or moves in the night and the day belongs to Allah.
- He is the All-Hearing and All-Knowing.
- The mystical reading speaks of night and day as light and darkness, and of the heart as held by God alone.

14.text:
The verse commands the Prophet ﷺ to declare his exclusive worship of Allah. "Say, O Prophet, 'Will I take any guardian other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, Who provides for all and is not in need of provision?' Say, 'I have been commanded to be the first to submit and not be one of the polytheists.'" The disbelievers asked the Prophet ﷺ to take a guardian other than Allah. The answer is that Allah is the Creator of the heavens and earth, who gives provision to His servants and is not in need of them.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Say, 'Will I take any guardian other than Allah'"** is the question put to the idolaters. They worship idols and other things together with Allah. Does it make sense? Indeed. that I take any one other than Allah as a guardian and a protector from whom I seek help? "Do you order me to worship other than Allah, O you fools?" (39:64). "I created not the Jinn and humans except that they should worship Me" (51:56). The oneness of Allah is the point. Makkah was where this was said.

**"the Originator of the heavens and the earth"** means Allah is the One Who created the heavens and the earth without any precedent. There was no Creator before Him.

**"Who provides for all and is not in need of provision"** means He is the One Who gives provision to whichever of His servants He wishes. None of His servants provide for Him. He is not in any need of His servants. His servants are in need of Him. He feeds but is not fed. Indeed. To Him belongs the attribute of generosity, so He feeds. To Him belongs the rightful due of eternity, so He is not fed. Indeed.

**"Say, 'I have been commanded to be the first to submit'"** means my Lord has instructed me to be the first one from this nation to submit and be humble. I am ordered to be the first of those who submit themselves to Allah as Muslims from this Ummah.

**"and not be one of the polytheists"** means He has prohibited me from being of those who associate others as partners with Him. Do not be among those who associate others with Him.

### The mystical reading

The mystical reading asks: after He has honored me with His beautiful friendship, shall I take another as friend? Indeed. After the brightness of His solicitude has fallen upon me, shall I gaze on someone else in the two houses? The sun of solicitude and kind favor has shone upon me from the Majestic and Exalted Threshold. It took care of my business without me in the two worlds. It lit up my heart with the eternal love. It adorned it with the ornament of intimacy. Indeed. He gave me such eminence at the forefront of acceptance that sometimes He puts up with my disdain: "By thy life!" (15:72). Sometimes the grasp of the attributes explains the polish of my heart's mirror by virtue of solicitude: "Did We not expand for thee thy breast?" (94:1). Sometimes the assessor of the beginningless and endless register turns over the acceptance and rejection of the creatures to my threshold: "Whatever the Messenger gives you, take; whatever he prohibits you, forgo" (59:7). With all this good fortune, rank, solicitude, and kind favor, indeed, how would it be appropriate for my heart to request someone else or to gaze upon this world and the afterworld? Indeed. So be it. Hence he said concerning this world, "What do I have to do with this world?" And concerning the afterworld: "The eyesight did not swerve, nor did it exceed" (53:17). Neither this world nor the afterworld. Rather, seeing the Patron. That is the goal. The Originator of the heavens and earth. The God who created earth and heaven. Indeed. He is the enactor of the world and the world's folk. Indeed. The knower of the apparent and the hidden. He does not partake of daily provision. He assigns daily provision to the servants.

### In short

- The Prophet ﷺ will not take any guardian other than Allah.
- Allah is the Originator of the heavens and earth and provides for all.
- He has commanded the Prophet ﷺ to be the first to submit.
- The Prophet ﷺ is forbidden from being among the polytheists.
- The mystical reading speaks of God's friendship as enough for the heart.

15.text:
The verse adds a warning. "Say, 'I truly fear, if I were to disobey my Lord, the torment of a tremendous Day.'" In the previous verses, the command given was to shun shirk and believe in the perfect power of Allah mentioned therein. In this verse, the punishment for the contravention of this command has been mentioned in a particularly endearing manner. The Prophet ﷺ has been commanded to tell the people something. Should he too come to contravene the command of his Lord, then he too has the fear. The fear is of the punishment. It is of the Day of Qiyamah. So be it. It is obvious that the noble Messenger of Allah is divinely protected from every sin. Indeed. So the likelihood of disobedience coming from him simply does not exist. Indeed. But by mentioning this hypothetical situation, the purpose is to convey the message to the community. The contravention of the Divine command is so serious a matter. Even the greatest prophet cannot stand excused from it. If not him, who else?

### Phrase by phrase

**"Say, 'I truly fear'"** means the Prophet ﷺ is to say that he knows and fears. "Do you order me to worship other than Allah, O you fools?" (39:64). "I created not the Jinn and humans except that they should worship Me" (51:56). Jalla Sha'nuhu is the One feared. Tawhid is the command.

**"if I were to disobey my Lord"** means if I go against Allah by committing that which He has prohibited. Indeed. Such as associating partners with Him, indeed. Or by leaving out what He has instructed me to do, indeed. Such as having faith and doing good actions. So be it.

**"the torment of a tremendous Day"** means the punishment on the Day of Qiyamah, the Day of Resurrection. I would face then a tremendous torment on an awful Day.

### In short

- The Prophet ﷺ is commanded to say he fears the torment of a tremendous Day.
- The hypothetical disobedience shows the seriousness of contravening the Divine command.
- Even the greatest prophet cannot stand excused from the Divine command.

16.text:
The verse closes with mercy. "Whoever is spared the torment of that Day will have certainly been shown Allah's mercy. And that is the absolute triumph." The punishment of the Day of Resurrection is extremely horrendous and harsh. Whoever finds this removed from him or her should know that it was great mercy from Allah. Deliverance from punishment and admittance into Paradise are inseparable from each other. The word "success" means being admitted into Jannah (Paradise). This tells us that deliverance from punishment and admittance into Paradise are inseparable from each other.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Whoever is spared the torment of that Day"** means the person from whom Allah keeps away and removes the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. "Do you order me to worship other than Allah, O you fools?" (39:64). "I created not the Jinn and humans except that they should worship Me" (51:56). Tawhid is the way. Al-Mahshar is the gathering place.

**"will have certainly been shown Allah's mercy"** means he has attained success through the mercy of Allah. He has been blessed with His mercy.

**"And that is the absolute triumph"** means such salvation and safety from the punishment is a clear victory which no other victory can equal. Success here indicates acquiring profit and negates loss. Whoever is moved away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise, he indeed is successful (3:185).

### In short

- Being spared the torment of that Day is Allah's mercy.
- Deliverance from punishment and admittance into Paradise go together.
- That is the absolute triumph, a clear victory which no other can equal.

17.text:
The verse states that Allah alone brings harm and benefit. "If Allah touches you with harm, none can undo it except Him. And if He touches you with a blessing, He is Most Capable of everything." Harm and good both come from Allah. No one can remove what He sends, and no one can withhold what He gives. This is a basic article of faith.

### Phrase by phrase

**"If Allah touches you with harm"** means affliction, hardship, or penury. No one can remove it but Allah.

**"none can undo it except Him"** means no one can lift the harm but Allah.

**"And if He touches you with a blessing"** means good fortune, blessing, or wealth. No one can stop Allah's grace.

19.text:
The verse challenges the idolaters to name the greatest witness and establishes the Quran as a warning. "Ask them, O Prophet, 'Who is the best witness?' Say, 'Allah is! He is a Witness between me and you. And this Quran has been revealed to me so that, with it, I may warn you and whoever it reaches. Do you pagans testify that there are other gods besides Allah?' Then say, 'I will never testify to this!' And say, 'There is only One God. And I totally reject whatever idols you associate with Him.'"

### Phrase by phrase

**"Ask them, O Prophet, 'Who is the best witness?'"** means: what thing is the most great in witness? The answer is Allah. He is the greatest and most honoured witness. He is a witness between you and me. He knows what I have brought to you and how you respond.

**"Allah is! He is a Witness between me and you"** means Allah knows what I brought you and what you will answer me with. One commentary says there is no bearing witness more truthful than the Real's own bearing witness to what He witnessed at the first. That is His words, "God bears witness that there is no god but He" (3:18). This is the Real's bearing witness that the Real is the Real. Abū ʿAbdallāh Qurashī said this is a teaching for the servants and a right guidance for the seekers. Put aside the path of resistance, lest you fall into the pit like the abandoned Iblis.

One commentary says God bears witness to His oneness, His unity, and His self-sufficiency. Others assent to the truth of that to which He bears witness concerning Himself. He Himself bore witness to His lordship, greatness, and oneness, for no one else was worthy. The creatures cannot reach the core of His majesty. Jaʿfar ibn MuḤammad said the bearing witness of people is built on four pillars: following commands, avoiding prohibitions, contentment, and approval. People's bearing witness is of three sorts: the common people emerge from associationism, the elect enter contemplation, and the elect of the elect receive the breeze of companionship. The self-purifier sees all from Him. The recognizer sees all in Him. The tawhid-voicer sees all as He.

**"And this Quran has been revealed to me so that, with it, I may warn you and whoever it reaches"** means the Quran is a warner for all who hear of it. One commentary says Gabriel brought down this Quran. One commentary says it was revealed to me that I may warn you, people of Makkah, and whomever it may reach among men and jinn. One commentary says the Prophet ﷺ is the Last Prophet and the Quran will keep reaching until the Day of Qiyamah. It will continue to be recited and taught right through the Day of Qiyamah. Sayyidna Said ibn Jubayr said: to whomever the Quran has reached, he has become like one who has visited Muhammad ﷺ. Another hadith says: to whomever the Quran has reached, I am his warner. The Prophet ﷺ asked his Companions emphatically to convey his instructions and teachings to people, even if it be one ayah. Abdullah ibn Masud reports that the Prophet ﷺ praised those who convey his sayings to the Ummah.

Ar-Rabi' bin Anas said those who follow the Messenger ought to call to what he called to. Allah said next: "But those of the sects that reject it, the Fire will be their promised meeting place" (11:17).

**"Do you pagans testify that there are other gods besides Allah?"** is the question put to the idolaters. "I will never testify to this" is the Prophet's answer. Similarly, in another ayah, Allah said: "Then if they testify, testify not you with them" (6:150).

**"There is only One God. And I totally reject whatever idols you associate with Him"** means He is one God, the only one worthy of worship, who has no partners, sharers, or associates in His pristine Divinity. I am free from all that you associate as partners with Him.

The event of revelation: a deputation of the people of Makkah came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked for a witness. Thereupon the verse was revealed. The witness of Allah refers to those miracles and signs which Allah made manifest to confirm the veracity of the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ. Addressing the people of Makkah, it was said: Do you stand to witness against Allah by saying that there are other gods along with Allah? If that is so, you are responsible for your fate. As for me, I bear no such witness.

Tawhid is the point. The path of the Quran is the path of oneness. Migration and the description of the Ummah are part of the good news the previous prophets gave. The verse is about the best witness and the warning to all who hear.

### In short

20.text:
The verse says the People of the Book recognize the Prophet as they recognize their own children. "Those to whom We gave the Scripture recognize him to be a true prophet as they recognize their own children. Those who have ruined themselves will never believe."

### Phrase by phrase

**"Those to whom We gave the Scripture"** means those to whom We gave the knowledge of the Torah and the Injil. One commentary names Abdullah ibn Salam and his followers, and contrasts them with Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and his followers. One commentary says the Jews who were given the Torah and the Christians who were given the Gospel recognize the Prophet Muhammad completely, just as they recognize their own children from other children. One commentary says those to whom We have given the Scripture recognize him by the descriptions of him in their Scripture as they recognize their sons.

**"recognize him to be a true prophet as they recognize their own children"** means the People of the Book know him well. This is because they received good news from the previous Messengers about the coming of Muhammad ﷺ. The Torah and Injil carry a full description of the physical features of the Prophet ﷺ, his home city, his post-emigration place of residence, his habits and morals and achievements, all in such detail that it leaves no room for doubt. In fact, the Torah and Injil carry even the detailed description of his noble Sahabah. Therefore, there was no possibility that anyone who recited the Torah and Injil and believed in them would be unable to recognize the Prophet ﷺ.

The simile is of children, not of parents recognizing children, because the recognition of children by parents is most detailed and certain. Children remain before parents day and night under all conditions. So parents recognize their children better than children recognize their parents.

Sayyidna Abdullah ibn Salam belonged to the Jewish faith, then he became a Muslim. Sayyidna Faruq al-A'zam asked him why the People of the Book recognize the Prophet as their own sons. Abdullah ibn Salam said: We know the Holy Prophet ﷺ from his qualities and features revealed by Allah Almighty through the Torah. This knowledge is certain and absolute.

Sayyidna Zayd ibn Sa'nah, who first belonged to the People of the Book, recognized the Prophet ﷺ through the Torah and the Injil. He tested one quality: his forbearance dominates his anger. He found it true and became a Muslim.

**"Those who have ruined themselves will never believe"** means those who have brought loss to themselves by disbelief will not believe. They have lost their own souls.

One commentary says people do not accept the truth because of the fear of some immediate loss. The cost of acceptance is that man must give up status and ready-made advantages. When a man is not ready to make these sacrifices, he does not accept the truth. He pushes himself into eternal loss for instant gain. On the Day of Judgment, when all the veils are torn asunder, he will see that all supports except that of God were false. He will contradict his own statements. The edifice of false beliefs will be destroyed.

The mystical reading says reality is familiar to man. It speaks the same silent language throughout the universe. The Jews and Christians had heralded the advent of the last Prophet. In spite of things being so clear, people do not accept the truth because of the fear of some immediate loss.

### In short

- The People of the Book recognize the Prophet as they recognize their own children.
- The Torah and Injil describe him in detail.
- Abdullah ibn Salam and Zayd ibn Sa'nah recognized him and became Muslim.
- Those who ruin themselves by disbelief will not believe.
- Refusal of truth is often driven by fear of losing status or advantage.
